objective: Decompose HYDRAGROW runtime boundaries without creating a second source of truth, while preserving authoritative configuration, command, telemetry, realtime, firmware contract, fleet analytics, and verification semantics.

acceptance.criterion: Backend configuration desired-state persistence has an explicit application-service boundary while PostgreSQL remains authoritative.
acceptance.verification: Configuration service unit test; backend clippy and targeted configuration tests

acceptance.criterion: ConfigurationSync retains durable lifecycle and bounded recovery semantics without introducing a second configuration authority.
acceptance.verification: Existing ConfigurationSync tests and cross-system evidence; review of configuration service and sync paths

acceptance.criterion: Realtime events route through a deterministic best-effort boundary and reconnect/malformed-frame recovery returns to authoritative query state.
acceptance.verification: Frontend realtimeRouter tests and backend WebSocket tests

acceptance.criterion: Frontend route/data boundaries isolate heavy views, normalize query keys, and preserve StationContext and React Query authority.
acceptance.verification: Frontend build, TypeScript, ESLint, and full Vitest suite

acceptance.criterion: Firmware MQTT topic/payload fixtures use the canonical shared contract and firmware ownership is explicit.
acceptance.verification: C++ sensor native fixture/build and controller target checks; Rust sensor target verification where toolchain permits

acceptance.criterion: Fleet comparison is bounded to 2–4 authorized devices and exports/proposals use existing fleet/configuration authorities.
acceptance.verification: Fleet backend tests and FleetView targeted tests

acceptance.criterion: Operational verification records synchronization/command lifecycle metrics and separates software evidence from physical HIL and production deployment evidence.
acceptance.verification: Metrics registration test and P2 evidence record
